title: The Drop of Marseille's old port
premise: Noor Eastwick, a deniable fixer for a shadowy embassy in Marseille, receives a calendar invitation from her handler, Elias Vann — sent after his body was pulled from the old port. The invitation places her at the Vieux-Port summit in three days, where France, Italy, and a third unnamed government will sign an intelligence-sharing pact built on a fabricated terror attack. Following the trail of Vann's last case, Noor discovers the bombing was staged by the pact's own architects, and that the assassin hired to erase loose ends is Karim Sadek, the man she once loved and betrayed. To expose the truth she must smuggle evidence past three governments' security services while dodging Karim, who has been ordered to kill her and cannot bring himself to do it. In the end, Noor burns her own cover to detonate the truth publicly at the summit; the pact collapses, Karim takes a fatal bullet meant for her, and Noor walks into the Mediterranean dawn with nothing but her name — finally her own.
about_author: Casper Eastwick is the pen name of a former maritime logistics consultant who spent a decade shuttling between Mediterranean ports before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers from a rented apartment above a Marseille fish market, claiming the smell keeps him honest.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She finishes scrubbing a diplomat's scandal in Marseille when her phone chimes: a meeting request from Elias Vann, timestamped tomorrow — two days after divers pulled his body from the old port. The beat is cold dread wrapped in professional calm; grief deferred, as always, for the job.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Calendar
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She breaks into Vann's shuttered office above the Quai du Port and finds his laptop still syncing: a folder labeled 'LANTERNE' containing photos of crates that never existed and a summit briefing marked EYES ONLY. Someone else searched the room before her. Beat: the first vertigo of realizing the conspiracy reaches upward.

chapters.title: The Embassy That Isn't
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She reports to her director, Madame Reyner, at the unmarked consulate on Rue Paradis, and is ordered to drop LANTERNE and shadow the Italian delegation instead. Noor obeys — and copies the folder first. Beat: loyalty cracking against instinct; the reader sees her choose herself without admitting it.

chapters.title: Crates of Air
chapters.summary: Dual POV opens with Karim Sadek arriving in Marseille under a Belgian passport, receiving his target list: three names, one of them Noor's. His POV shows a man who kills cleanly and feels nothing — until he reads her name. Beat: the antagonist becomes human, and therefore dangerous in a new way.

chapters.title: Fish Market Alibi
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Working the docks, she finds the warehouse where the 'terror' shipment was supposedly stored: empty for eighteen months, yet officially logged as seized explosives. A dockworker who talks to her is found floating by morning. Beat: guilt sharpens into resolve; the cost of asking questions is now blood.

chapters.title: Three Flags, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Through intercepted cables and a bribed archivist, Noor maps how the staged bombing justified the intelligence pact — each government supplied a piece of the fiction. Meanwhile Karim eliminates name number one. Beat: the conspiracy's scale lands; the reader understands no institution will save her.

chapters.title: What Vann Knew
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A retired contact of Vann's, dying of cancer, gives her a cassette: Vann recorded his own warning, naming Deputy Director Aubert as the pact's architect and predicting his own death. Beat: grief finally arrives, raw and unusable, transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Rooftop of Saints
chapters.summary: Karim's POV. He corners Noor on the Notre-Dame de la Garde terraces at dusk — and lets her go, falsifying his report. Their first exchange in six years is four sentences long and says everything. Beat: love against duty made literal; both leave knowing the next meeting won't be merciful.

chapters.title: The Reyner Problem
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Reyner confronts her with evidence of the copied folder and offers a choice: become the embassy's scapegoat or hand over LANTERNE. Noor stalls, then realizes Reyner is terrified — not of Aubert, but of being next. Beat: the mentor figure revealed as another survivor in the machine.

chapters.title: Ghost Frequency
chapters.summary: Karim's POV. Ordered to accelerate, he instead feeds Noor a warning through an old signal channel they used in Beirut. She almost doesn't trust it; she goes anyway, and finds name number two already dead — she was meant to be standing there. Beat: wary alliance forming inside mutual betrayal.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Price
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The bribed archivist demands extraction for the original staging orders signed by all three governments. Noor arranges it through channels that burn half her network. Beat: the price of survival made concrete — every truth costs her a piece of the life she built.

chapters.title: Interlude: The Port at Night
chapters.summary: Split POV, near-wordless. Noor and Karim meet by accident at the water's edge, both unable to sleep, both armed. They talk about Beirut, about the life neither chose. No one draws. Beat: the quiet center of the book; tenderness as the most subversive act available to them.

chapters.title: Aubert's Dinner
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Summoned to a private dinner with Deputy Director Aubert, she plays the loyal fixer while he describes, pleasantly, what happened to Vann. She leaves with the confirmation she needed and a tail she can't shake. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; the villain's charm is more frightening than menace.

chapters.title: Burning the Network
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She distributes copies of the evidence to journalists, a magistrate, and a dead-drop for the Italians — insurance against her own death. Reyner quietly looks away, choosing survival over obedience. Beat: point of no return; Noor stops being an instrument and becomes an actor.

chapters.title: The Tail
chapters.summary: Karim's POV. Aubert's second assassin shadows Noor through Panier alleys; Karim intercepts and kills him, then confesses everything to Noor — his contract, his falsified reports, his refusal. She doesn't forgive him. She plans with him anyway. Beat: love against duty resolved into partnership without absolution.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Security locks down the Vieux-Port; the three delegations arrive amid celebration. Noor's journalist contact is arrested, one copy of the evidence seized. Karim reports to Aubert one last time, wearing a wire for Noor. Beat: the walls closing in; hope reduced to a single narrow corridor.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Minutes
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Using summit accreditation Vann left her, she infiltrates the press gallery with the surviving evidence as the signing ceremony begins. Aubert spots her from the dais. Beat: rising panic into eerie calm — she has rehearsed this moment her whole career, just never as the defendant.

chapters.title: The Truth, Out Loud
chapters.summary: Climax, split POV. Noor hijacks the ceremony's live feed with the staging orders; delegates scatter, cameras roll, Aubert orders her silenced. Karim steps between the muzzle and her — takes the bullet meant for her heart, and drops Aubert's chief of security before falling. Beat: catharsis and devastation fused; duty finally broken by love.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Aubert is arrested by his own delegation to contain the damage; the pact dies in committee within a week. Noor testifies from behind glass, name redacted, then walks out of the courthouse having refused witness protection. Beat: hollow victory; justice achieved outside the law, at a price no court can weigh.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She scatters Vann's cassette tape and Karim's Belgian passport from the rocks below Notre-Dame de la Garde. Reyner sends one message: the embassy never existed, so neither does her resignation. Beat: mourning without ceremony; letting the institutions keep their fictions while she keeps the truth.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Offered a new identity by a grateful magistrate, she declines — signs her real name to a statement releasing the full LANTERNE file publicly, ending her usefulness to every service at once. Beat: liberation through self-destruction of the false self; freedom as the final act of defiance.

chapters.title: The Drop
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Noor's POV. Months later she runs a small shipping consultancy at the old port, unremarkable and free. A stranger leaves a coffee cup on her table — inside, a note in Karim's handwriting, dated before the summit: 'If you're reading this, live loudly.' She smiles at the water. Beat: quiet, earned peace; the drop of the title — a single moment of grace the sea returns to her.
